ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the sinusoidal AC source is connected between the left and right two terminals; between these two terminals there are two parallel branches. The upper branch consists of a capacitor labeled 100 μF in series with a resistor R; the lower branch consists of an inductor labeled 0.02 H in series with another identical resistor R. Reasoning: Write the total admittance according to the two parallel series branches in the figure: Y = 1/(R - j/(ωC)) + 1/(R + jωL). Respectively, Y_RC = (R + j/(ωC))/(R^2 + 1/(ω^2 C^2)), Y_RL = (R - jωL)/(R^2 + ω^2 L^2). To make the total admittance a pure conductance at all frequencies, the imaginary part must always be zero, so the positive imaginary part of the RC branch equals the magnitude of the negative imaginary part of the RL branch: [1/(ωC)]/[R^2 + 1/(ω^2 C^2)] = [ωL]/[R^2 + ω^2 L^2]. Cross-multiply and require it to hold for all ω, match the constant term and the ω^2 term, obtaining R^2 = L/C. Therefore R = sqrt(L/C) = sqrt(0.02 / (100×10^-6)) = sqrt(200) = 14.142... Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a source feeding two parallel series branches: RC on top and RL on bottom, with equal resistors R. Write the total admittance as Y = 1/(R - j/(omega C)) + 1/(R + j omega L). Rationalize each branch admittance. Equate the positive imaginary part of the RC branch to the negative imaginary part of the RL branch. Since this equality must hold at every frequency, match the constant and omega-squared coefficients after cross-multiplication. This yields R^2=L/C, so substitute C=100 microfarad and L=0.02 H to obtain R=14.14 ohms.

Ω。

method.method_draft: After identifying the parallel RC-series and RL-series branches in the image, work in the s-domain instead of immediately using j omega. Express the top-branch admittance as sC/(1+sRC) and the bottom-branch admittance as 1/(R+sL). Look for the condition that makes the two denominators share the same factor, so the total admittance has complete pole-zero cancellation and becomes a constant conductance. Setting sL = sR^2C gives L=R^2C; with this condition Y simplifies exactly to 1/R for all s, hence for all sinusoidal frequencies. Substitute L=0.02 H and C=100 microfarad to get R=14.14 ohms.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中正弦交流源接在一个两端网络上；网络内部有上下两个并联支路。上支路由一个标注为 100 μF 的电容与一个电阻 R 串联组成；下支路由一个标注为 0.02 H 的电感与另一个电阻 R 串联组成。

推理：按指定方法在 s 域分析。上支路阻抗为 R + 1/(sC)，所以其导纳为 Y_1 = sC/(1 + sRC)。下支路阻抗为 R + sL，所以其导纳为 Y_2 = 1/(R + sL)。总导纳为 Y = sC/(1+sRC) + 1/(R+sL)。若要总导纳在所有频率下都是纯电导，需要发生完全极零抵消，使结果成为常数。令下支路分母 R+sL 与上支路分母 1+sRC 具有相同因子：R+sL = R(1+sRC)，因此 sL = sR^2C，即 L = R^2 C。于是 Y = sC/(1+sRC) + 1/[R(1+sRC)] = (sC + 1/R)/(1+sRC) = (1/R)(1+sRC)/(1+sRC) = 1/R，为常数纯电导。代入 L = 0.02 H，C = 100 μF = 100×10^-6 F，得到 R = sqrt(L/C) = sqrt(0.02/(100×10^-6)) = sqrt(200) = 14.14 Ω。
